**Rules that constrain how AI is used here — these bind this agent:**

- **D5 concept location must be done by the human first, without AI.** The spec is explicit:
  "Find the relevant code yourself first, without AI ... Then confirm with AI ... This order
  matters." So when Zach is working a D5 issue, **do not locate the code for him** — wait until

  points are lost if he cannot explain his own PR.
- **Branch names**: `feat/issue-<n>-<slug>` or `fix/issue-<n>-<slug>`.
  **Commit messages**: the spec's own example is `feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)` —
  **Conventional Commits**, matching `AGENTS.md`, and *contradicting* the team's draft
  `standards.md` ("Add …"). The course spec and `main` agree; the draft is the outlier.
- **PRs**: link the issue with `Closes #<n>`, tests written/updated, reviewed by a teammate with
  an actual comment, CI passing (CI not required for Sprint 0). `main` is branch-protected.
- **AI logs** are captured with **SpecStory**, not written by hand.

### Settled: how AI logs are captured (D4)

Syllabus §16: "An AI log is the record of an AI conversation with an AI tool — the prompts,
responses, and tool used. Logs are pushed to the team's GitHub repository rather than submitted
separately, and **referenced from the related GitHub issue**." Separately, "for each issue or
sprint, include a short written rationale (in the pull request description or sprint report)
explaining how AI output was used, especially when a suggestion was modified or rejected."
So the log is the **transcript**; the rationale is a different artifact and lives in the PR/report.

**The authoritative spec is <https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/>** (read 2026-09-14) — not
`ai-logs/README.md`, which only summarises it and links a `docs/sprints.md` that exists on no
ref. Requirements, verbatim where it matters:

**SpecStory is installed** (`~/.local/bin/specstory`, v2.10.0) and — importantly — **sessions

otherwise hard after the fact:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
specstory list claude                                  # sessions for THIS directory
specstory sync -s <session-id> --output-dir <dir> --local-time-zone
```

Two gotchas, both verified 2026-09-14:

- **Sessions are bucketed by the directory the session ran in.** A session run inside
  `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` is **not** listed from the repo root — run `specstory list` from
  the same directory the session used, or it looks like the log does not exist.
- **A sync is a snapshot.** Re-run it at the end of a session, or the log stops partway.

**Before committing any transcript, scan it for secrets (R16).** SpecStory redacts by default,

## Invariants — how things work; do not break these

Each cites the repo rule that owns it. Break one and it still compiles.

- **`select`, never `include`, in Prisma queries; `credential.key` never leaves a query** —
  `agents/rules/data-prefer-select-over-include.md`, `AGENTS.md`.
- **No business logic in repositories; no Prisma outside them** —
  `agents/rules/data-repository-pattern.md`.
- **Package layering is acyclic**: `lib` → `app-store` → `features` → `trpc` → `apps/web` —
  `agents/rules/architecture-circular-dependencies.md`.
- **`packages/features/**` must not import `@calcom/trpc`** —
  `agents/rules/architecture-features-modules.md`.
- **`apps/api/v2` imports features/trpc only via `@calcom/platform-libraries`** — `AGENTS.md`.
- **Permission checks in `page.tsx`, never `layout.tsx`** — `AGENTS.md`.
- **Never edit `*.generated.ts`** — `agents/rules/patterns-app-store.md`.
- **No breaking changes to v1/v2 endpoints; version instead** —
  `agents/rules/api-no-breaking-changes.md`.
- **All UI strings via `t()` and `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`** — `AGENTS.md`.

## Known API facts and quirks

Platform behaviour learned the hard way, with citations — including disproofs of anything in
`AGENTS.md`, `agents/rules/**` or `students.md` (R5: record the disproof, name the file and
line it corrects).

- **CI is label- and path-gated.** A docs/Markdown-only PR runs no checks and `required` still
  passes; without `ready-for-e2e` no build or e2e job runs at all — `.github/workflows/pr.yml`,
  verified 2026-09-14.
- **`yarn test` does not run the timezone project.** CI runs the suite a second time with
  `VITEST_MODE=timezone`; the selection happens at `vitest.workspace.ts:7` — verified
  2026-09-14.
- **Next.js is 16.2.3, not 14.** `apps/web/package.json` `dependencies.next` = `16.2.3`,
  verified 2026-09-14. This **disproves** `students.md` ("Next.js 14", with a link to the
  Next 14 docs) and `AGENTS.md` §Tech Stack ("Next.js 13+"). Both are stale; neither is ours
  to edit (R13). Treat any framework-version claim in those two files as a lead only (R3).
- **API v2 is NestJS** — `apps/api/v2/package.json` depends on `@nestjs/common` et al.,
  verified 2026-09-14.
- **Correction: a database *is* possible here.** This file previously said no DB-backed work
  could run because Docker is absent. Homebrew has `postgresql@14` (14.18) installed with
  `postgres`, `pg_ctl` and `initdb` on PATH — it is simply not started, and nothing is listening
  on the `.env` default port 5450. So **D1 (run the app locally) is achievable** without Docker;
  it needs Postgres started, the `calendso` database created, migrations applied and a seed.
  Verified 2026-09-14.
- **`docs/sprint0/standards.md` is @lexzach's (Zachary Bowden), on his open WIP PR #7.** It is a
  shared team deliverable (D3, one per team), so changes belong there as review suggestions or
  Zulip coordination — **do not push to that branch**. A drafted Definition of Done plus the two
  conflict fixes are in `docs/agent/proposed-definition-of-done.md` (private, uncommitted).
- **The team's standards exist, unmerged, on PR #7.** `docs/sprint0/standards.md` on branch
  `docs/standards-guidelines` (opened 2026-09-13, still titled `WIP:`) covers branch names
  (`docs|feat|fix`/`name`), commit names (present tense, `Add …`), PR process, testing
  expectations, AI tool use and a **Definition of Done heading with no content**. It says
  nothing about AI-log links. Verified 2026-09-14 — and because it is `WIP:`, its own rule says
  it is not to be reviewed for merging, so **none of it binds yet**. Three conflicts with rules
  live on `main` are recorded in `docs/AGENT-PRACTICES.md` §Posture.
- **Branch `short` does not match the proposed branch convention** (`docs|feat|fix`/`name`).
  Harmless while PR #7 is unmerged, but a future branch should be e.g. `docs/agent-standard`.
- **The AI-log deliverable has a documented shape** (`ai-logs/README.md`, tracked, added in
  `02e09b9cb3`): `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<github-username>/YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-description>.md`,
  with a sibling directory of the same name for attachments; the tool id for this tool is
  `claude-code`. **But the instructions it defers to do not exist**: it links
  `docs/sprints.md#d4--ai-tooling-setup`, and `docs/sprints.md` is on no ref (verified
  2026-09-14, `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- docs/sprints.md`); the relative path in that
  link (`../../docs/`) also points above the repo root. **Correction to this file's earlier
  claim** that the repo documented no course conventions: it does, and the grep that "proved"
  otherwise searched for words the file does not contain (R4).
- **`yarn build` writes to your database. It is not read-only.** `packages/prisma`'s build
  script is `ts-node --transpile-only ./auto-migrations.ts`, and `auto-migrations.ts:34` runs
  **`yarn prisma migrate deploy`** against whatever `DATABASE_URL` is set to. `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  §Building tells every contributor to run `yarn build` before pushing, and says nothing about
  this. **Never run `yarn build` with `.env` pointed at a shared, staging or production
  database** — it will apply pending migrations to it.
- **`yarn build`'s "no database, skip gracefully" guard does not work.**
  `auto-migrations.ts` intends to skip when the DB is absent, but
  `is-prisma-available-check.ts` returns `false` only for `Prisma.PrismaClientInitializationError`
  and **rethrows every other error**. A refused connection to a Postgres that is not running is
  not that class, so it escapes the guard, reaches `main().catch()` and exits 1. Net effect on a
  machine with no Docker: the documented pre-push command **fails in 20s** at
  `@calcom/prisma#build` with ``Invalid `prisma.$queryRaw()` invocation``, and the failure looks
  like a code problem when it is an environment one. Escape hatch: `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1`
  (`auto-migrations.ts:17`). Verified 2026-09-14.
- **A nested worktree doubles the test suite and turns it red — measured.** With a worktree at
  `.claude/worktrees/`, `TZ=UTC yarn test` from the primary checkout reported **830 files (208
  failed) / 6323 tests (38 failed), exit 1**. The identical tree with `--exclude '**/.claude/**'`
  reported **406 files (0 failed) / 4119 tests (0 failed), exit 0**. All 208 "failures" were
  duplicate copies, 202 of them `(0 test)` import errors because the nested checkout has source
  but no `node_modules`. `vitest list` also exits 1 in that state. Verified 2026-09-14.
  **Check `git worktree list` before trusting a test count.**
- **`CLAUDE.local.md` IS loaded by this harness.** Confirmed 2026-09-14: a session restart
  re-read instruction files and listed `/Users/zachshort/Projects/cal.diy/CLAUDE.local.md` as
  "user's private project instructions, not checked in". The private router works where it is;
  it does not need to move into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
- **`yarn lint` is turbo-cached and the documented command has no `--force`** — it can print
  `>>> FULL TURBO` having executed nothing. Use `yarn lint --force` when the number matters.
  See §Environment. Verified 2026-09-14.
- **Nested worktrees live inside the repo.** Claude Code puts them at
  `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`, i.e. *inside* `~/Projects/cal.diy`. Git ignores that path
  (`.git/info/exclude`), but tools that glob the filesystem do not necessarily. Test output on
  2026-09-14 showed vitest reporting files under `.claude/worktrees/.../apps/...` while running
  from the primary checkout. `type-check` and `lint` are **not** affected — turbo scopes them to
  the `workspaces` globs in `package.json` (`apps/*`, `packages/*`, ...), none of which match
  `.claude/worktrees/**`.
- **`turbo run type-check:ci` replays cached results**; `--force` is why `AGENTS.md` prescribes
  it.

# Contributing to Cal.diy

> **Important:** Cal.diy is a community-driven, open-source fork of Cal.com. Contributions made here **do not** get merged into Cal.com's production service — Cal.com is now closed-source. This repo is maintained independently by the community under the MIT license.

Contributions are what make the open source community such an amazing place to learn, inspire, and create. Any contributions you make are **greatly appreciated**.

## House Rules (for PRs and Issues)

### 👥 Prevent Work Duplication

Before submitting a new issue or PR, check if it already exists in the [Issues](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/issues) or [Pull Requests](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/pulls).

### ✅ Work Only on Approved Issues

For feature requests, please wait for a core team member to approve and remove the `🚨 needs approval` label before you start coding or submitting a PR.

For bugs, security, performance, documentation, etc., you can start coding immediately—even if the `🚨 needs approval` label is present.

We highly value new feature ideas, but to maintain consistency in the product direction, they must go through a review and approval process.

### 🚫 Don’t Just Drop a Link

Avoid posting third-party links (e.g., Slack threads or Linear tickets) without context. A GitHub issue or PR should stand on its own—reviewers shouldn’t have to chase information across multiple tools to understand the context.

### 👀 Think Like a Reviewer

Put yourself in the reviewer’s shoes. What would you want to know if reading this for the first time? Are there key decisions, goals, or constraints that need clarification? Does the PR assume knowledge that isn’t obvious? Are there related issues or previous PRs that should be linked?

### 🧵 Bring in Context from Private Channels

If the task originated from a private conversation (e.g., Slack), take a moment to extract the relevant details and include them in the GitHub issue or PR. Avoid sharing sensitive information, but make sure important reasoning is captured.

> Example:  
> “A user requested feature X to solve problem Y. I considered approaches A, B, and C, but chose C for the following reasons…”

### 📚 Treat It Like Documentation

GitHub is a shared source of truth. Every issue and PR contributes to the long-term understanding of the codebase. Write clearly enough that someone—possibly you—can revisit it months later and still understand what happened and why.

### ✅ Summarize Your PR at the Top

Even if the code changes are minor or self-explanatory, a short written summary helps reviewers quickly understand the intent. You can use GitHub Copilot’s auto-summarize feature, but make sure to verify it for accuracy and relevance.

### 🔗 Use GitHub Keywords to Auto-Link Issues

Use phrases like “Closes #123” or “Fixes #456” in your PR descriptions. This automatically links your PR to the related issue and closes it once merged—keeping everything traceable and organized.

### 🧪 Mention What Was Tested (and How)

Explain how you validated your changes. It doesn’t need to be exhaustive—just enough to give reviewers confidence that things were tested and work as expected.

> Example:  
> “Tested locally with mock data and confirmed the flow works on staging.”

### 🧠 Assume Future-You Won’t Remember

Write with the future in mind. If there are trade-offs, edge cases, or temporary workarounds, document them clearly so they don’t get lost or misinterpreted later.

## File Naming Conventions

To ensure consistency and make files easy to fuzzy-find, we follow the naming conventions below for **services**, **repositories**, and other class-based files.

### Repository Files

- Repository class files must include the `Repository` suffix.
- If the repository is backed by a specific technology (e.g. Prisma), prefix the filename and class name with it.
- File name must match the exported class exactly (PascalCase).

**Pattern:**

`Prisma<Entity>Repository.ts`

**Examples:**

```ts
// File: PrismaAppRepository.ts
export class PrismaAppRepository { ... }

// File: PrismaMembershipRepository.ts
export class PrismaMembershipRepository { ... }
```

This avoids ambiguous filenames like app.ts and improves discoverability in editors.

### Service Files

- Service class files must include the Service suffix.
- File name should be in PascalCase, matching the exported class.
- Keep naming specific — avoid generic names like AppService.ts.

**Pattern:**

`<Entity>Service.ts`

**Examples:**

```ts
// File: MembershipService.ts
export class MembershipService { ... }

// File: HashedLinkService.ts
export class HashedLinkService { ... }
```

**Note:**

- New files must avoid dot-suffixes like .service.ts or .repository.ts; these will be migrated from the existing codebase progressively.
- We still reserve suffixes such as .test.ts, .spec.ts, and .types.ts for their respective use cases.

## Linting

```

## Making a Pull Request

### Keep PRs Small and Focused

Large PRs are difficult to review and more prone to errors. We strongly encourage smaller, self-contained PRs:

- **Size limits**: Keep PRs under 500 lines of code changed and under 10 code files modified (excludes documentation, lock files, and auto-generated files)
- **Single responsibility**: Each PR should address one concern (one feature, one bug fix, or one refactor)
- **Split large changes**: If your task requires extensive changes, break it into multiple PRs that can be reviewed and merged independently

**How to split large changes:**
- Separate database/schema changes from application logic
- Split frontend and backend changes when possible
- Do preparatory refactoring in a separate PR before adding new features
- Create PRs in dependency order (infrastructure first, then features)

### PR Checklist

- Be sure to [check the "Allow edits from maintainers" option](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork) when creating your PR. (This option isn't available if you're [contributing from a fork belonging to an organization](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/5634))
- If your PR refers to or fixes an issue, add `refs #XXX` or `fixes #XXX` to the PR description. Replace `XXX` with the respective issue number. See more about [linking a pull request to an issue](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue).
- Fill out the PR template accordingly.
- Review the [App Contribution Guidelines](./packages/app-store/CONTRIBUTING.md) when building integrations.
- Lastly, make sure to keep your branches updated (e.g., click the `Update branch` button on the GitHub PR page).

## Verdict: right file, right button — and the fix isn't there

You found the save button. It's the only one in the codebase:

```
grep -rn 'data-testid="update-eventtype"' apps packages
```

returns exactly one source hit — [EventTypeLayout.tsx:280](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:280). The other six hits are Playwright specs driving it. So there's no second save button hiding in a mobile dropdown or a platform variant; the one you're looking at is the one in the video.

Here it is, [EventTypeLayout.tsx:273-283](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:273):

```tsx
<Button
  ref={saveButtonRef}
  className="ml-4 lg:ml-0"
  type="submit"
  loading={isUpdateMutationLoading}
  disabled={!formMethods.formState.isDirty}   // <- line 279
  data-testid="update-eventtype"
  form="event-type-form">
  {t("save")}
</Button>
```

**Line 279 is already the fix the issue asks for.** `disabled={!formMethods.formState.isDirty}` is precisely "grey the save button out until a field is touched." It's been there the whole time.

And it isn't a fake `disabled` that the design system swallows — [Button.tsx:242](packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx:242) does `const disabled = props.disabled || loading || false;` and passes it straight to the DOM element at [Button.tsx:353](packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx:353), with `disabled:opacity-30` in the variant classes. If `isDirty` were `false`, that button would be visibly greyed and unclickable.

## So what the bug actually is

Deduction, from the code above plus the reporter's screen recording: the button is enabled on load ⇒ `formMethods.formState.isDirty` is **already `true` before the user touches anything**.

The button isn't broken. It's faithfully reporting what the form told it. **You're one layer off** — the defect is in whatever *produces* that form state, not in the component that *consumes* it. `EventTypeLayout` here is a pure consumer: it receives `formMethods` as a prop ([EventTypeLayout.tsx:40](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:40), `formMethods: UseFormReturn<FormValues>`) and never creates it.

That reframes the whole PR, so it's worth saying plainly before you take the next guess: this is **not** "add a `disabled` prop." It's "stop the form from being born dirty." Different fix, different tests, and a much better PR to have to explain.

## Your next guess

Two things to aim it, both general react-hook-form behaviour rather than facts about this repo:

1. `isDirty` is not "has the user typed" — it's a **comparison of the form's current values against its `defaultValues`**. It flips to `true` the moment those two disagree, no keystroke required.
2. So there are two usual culprits, and they call for different fixes:
   - something runs `setValue(..., { shouldDirty: true })` during setup — note lines [143](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:143) and [267](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:267) in your own file use exactly that flag for the hidden-switch, so the pattern is in play here; or
   - the values the form is **initialised** with aren't equal to the values it **holds** once the event type's data is in — a shape mismatch (a field that arrives `null` and is normalised to `""`, a date that's a string one side and a `Date` the other, an object rebuilt on every render), so the very first post-load render already counts as "changed."

The thread to pull is in the snippet above: that button is bound to a form by id, `form="event-type-form"` ([line 281](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:281)). Follow that id to whoever declares the form and calls `useForm`, and see which of the two culprits it is. I'll confirm or disprove whatever you come back with.

**`EventTypeSingleLayout` is not a separate file.** It's the component declared *inside* the file you already named: [EventTypeLayout.tsx:52](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:52) (`function EventTypeSingleLayout({`), exported at [:331](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:331). So that half of the guess lands back on the same consumer — it takes `formMethods` as a prop and never creates it.

**"Wherever `useForm` is called" is the right answer.** Here's the full chain, each link cited:

| # | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [event-types/[type]/page.tsx:65](apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/event-types/[type]/page.tsx:65) | the route renders `<EventTypeWebWrapper …/>` |
| 2 | [EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:173](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:173) | `const { form, handleSubmit } = useEventTypeForm({ eventType, onSubmit: updateMutation.mutate });` |
| 3 | **[useEventTypeForm.ts:141](packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts:141)** | **`const form = useForm<FormValues>({ defaultValues, resolver: zodResolver(…) })`** — the call site |
| 4 | [useEventTypeForm.ts:42](packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts:42) | `const defaultValues: any = useMemo(() => ({ … }), [eventType, periodDates])` — ~70 fields mapped off `eventType` |
| 5 | [EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:341](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:341) → [EventType.tsx:102](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventType.tsx:102) | passed down as `formMethods`, and `<Form form={formMethods} id="event-type-form">` — the form your button's `form=` attribute points at |

Note the file lives in `packages/platform/atoms/`, not `apps/web/` — the web wrapper imports the hook from `@calcom/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm` ([EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:3](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:3)). Worth knowing before we touch it: **the platform atoms package shares this hook**, so a change here also lands on `EventTypePlatformWrapper`, which is the only other renderer of `<EventType` ([EventTypePlatformWrapper.tsx:410](packages/platform/atoms/event-types/wrappers/EventTypePlatformWrapper.tsx:410)). That's a blast-radius fact, not a blocker.

## What I have *not* established yet

I know where the form is born. I don't yet know **which** of the two mechanisms dirties it, and I'm not going to guess in a PR you have to defend line by line.

What I've ruled out so far:

- **Not a mount-time `setValue` on the default tab.** `?tabName` defaults to `setup`, and `EventSetupTab.tsx` contains **no `useEffect` at all** — every one of its nine `setValue(…, { shouldDirty: true })` calls sits inside an event handler (lines 157, 244, 251, 253, 289, 354, 355, 358, 359). Nothing there fires without a click.
- **Not the post-save `form.reset`.** The only `reset` in the wrapper is [EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:138](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:138), inside `updateMutation.onSuccess` — it runs *after* a save, not on load.

That leaves 79 `shouldDirty: true` call sites across 13 files in the editor, plus the shape-mismatch branch — `defaultValues` has several fields that look like normalisation candidates ([useEventTypeForm.ts:64](packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts:64) `description: eventType.description ?? undefined`, `:55` `lockedTimeZone: … || null`, `:78` `periodDates` rebuilt as a fresh object). Narrowing that by reading is guesswork; seeing `dirtyFields` on a real page settles it in one look.

**One design note that matters either way:** a hook-only unit test may *not* reproduce this. If the cause is a child component registering a field at a value that differs from `defaultValues`, rendering only `useEventTypeForm` in isolation would report `isDirty === false` and prove nothing. So I want the observation from a real page *before* I decide what the regression test asserts — otherwise we ship a test that passes for the wrong reason, which your own `agents/rules` calls out as not counting.

  if (result === "<p><br></p>") {
    result = "";

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-09-14 23:59:39-0400)**_

mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter would be apt here, but let me give you the diagnosis first.

## Root cause — proven on the live page, not inferred

**Repro** (`/event-types/12?tabName=setup`, freshly loaded, nothing touched):

```json
{ "buttonDisabled": false, "isDirty": true, "dirtyFields": { "description": true } }
```

Read straight out of React's fiber tree on your running app. One field, every time: **`description`**.

**Why it's dirty:**

```json
{ "defaultDescription": undefined, "currentDescription": "" }
```

- [useEventTypeForm.ts:64](packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts:64) sets the default to `description: eventType.description ?? undefined`. Every seeded event type has `description IS NULL` (verified in `psql`), so the default is `undefined`.
- Something then writes `""` into the live form. `undefined !== ""` ⇒ RHF flags it dirty ⇒ [EventTypeLayout.tsx:279](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:279) enables the button.

**Who writes it — the rich-text editor echoing its own initialisation:**

1. [ToolbarPlugin.tsx:386](packages/ui/components/editor/plugins/ToolbarPlugin.tsx:386) — a mount-time `useEffect(…, [])` seeds the Lexical editor from `getText()`.
2. That seeding is itself an `editor.update(…)`, and [ToolbarPlugin.tsx:410](packages/ui/components/editor/plugins/ToolbarPlugin.tsx:410) registers `editor.registerUpdateListener` inside the same effect — so the listener fires **immediately, on its own seeding update**, and calls `props.setText(html)`.
3. [EventSetupTab.tsx:153-158](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/setup/EventSetupTab.tsx:153) receives it and does `formMethods.setValue("description", markdownValue, { shouldDirty: true })`.

Nobody typed anything. The editor told the form "the description changed" because the editor finished loading.

## It is worse than the issue reports

The issue reads cosmetic. It isn't. I set a real markdown description on event type 12 in your **local seeded dev DB**, reloaded, and read the form (then reverted it — `id=12` is back to `description IS NULL`, confirmed):

| | value |
|---|---|
| stored / `defaultValues.description` | `**bold** and _italic_` |
| live `_formValues.description` after mount | `****bold**** and _italic_` |

**The asterisks double on load.** And since `handleSubmit` builds its payload from `dirtyValues` and submits only `if (dirtyFieldExists)` ([useEventTypeForm.ts:320](packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts:320), [:410](packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts:410)), `description` *is* in the payload — it's dirty. So pressing Save on an untouched event type doesn't no-op, it **writes a corrupted description back to the database**. That's the real cost of the bug, and it's a strong line for the PR body.

It also means the bug is **not** limited to empty descriptions — so the one-character fix is out.

## The fix options

One thing no option can deliver, and you should know before choosing: **"edit it, then edit it back ⇒ button greys out again" is not achievable here.** The markdown→HTML→markdown round-trip is lossy (I measured it: `- a\n- b` → `*   a\n*   b`, `Line one\nLine two` → `Line one<br>Line two`), so the restored value never equals the stored one. That's a separate bug. The achievable goal for #10 is the one the reporter asked for: **untouched form ⇒ greyed button.**

A companion one-liner worth taking with options 1 or 2: `?? undefined` → `?? ""` at [useEventTypeForm.ts:64](packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts:64), so that for the common empty-description case, edit-then-clear *does* return to clean.

**Which shape of fix do you want to defend in the PR?**

Options:
- **Ignore the mount echo in EventSetupTab (Recommended)** - A useRef guard in EventSetupTab.tsx: the editor's first setText after mount writes with shouldDirty:false, every later one keeps shouldDirty:true. ~4 lines, 1 file (+ the ?? "" companion = 2 files). Blast radius is the event-type setup tab only. Fixes the button for every description AND keeps the mangled value out of the save payload. Easiest to explain line-by-line, which Syllabus §16 requires of you. Risk: it assumes the mount echo always fires first — the test has to prove a real user edit still enables the button.
- **Stop the echo at the source in ToolbarPlugin** - Tag the seeding editor.update() and have the registered update listener skip that tagged update, so the editor never reports its own initialisation as a user change. Architecturally the correct fix and kills the whole class of bug. But it touches shared UI used by 6 <Editor> call sites (UserProfile, profile-view, DuplicateDialog, FormBuilder, EventSetupTab, CreateEventTypeForm), so I'd need to check none of them relies on that echo to populate its value — more review surface and more for you to defend.
- **Normalise the default only** - Change ?? undefined to ?? "" at useEventTypeForm.ts:64 and stop there. Smallest possible diff and it does close the reporter's exact repro, since every seeded event type has a NULL description. But I proved it insufficient: with a real markdown description the form still loads dirty (****bold****), so a reviewer who tests a described event type still sees the bug. I'd be arguing against this one in review.


**Answer:** Ignore the mount echo in EventSetupTab (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

```bash

/**
 * The Lexical editor behind the event type description calls `setText` twice while it mounts,
 * echoing back the value it was just seeded with. Writing that echo into the form is what let
 * users save an event type they had not touched: `md.render` -> `turndown` is lossy, so the echo
 * can differ from what is stored ("**bold**" comes back as "****bold****"), react-hook-form then
 * sees the form as changed, and the next save wrote the mangled text to the database.
 *
 * This guard answers one question per emission: is this the user editing, or the editor echoing?
 * It latches on the first differing value so that every later emission is treated as an edit -
 * including clearing the field back to the echoed text, which must still be saved.
 *
 * See https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/issues/10
 */
export function createDescriptionEditorGuard() {
  let mountEcho: string | null = null;
  let hasUserEdited = false;

  return function isUserEdit(markdownValue: string): boolean {
    if (hasUserEdited) return true;

    if (mountEcho === null) {
      mountEcho = markdownValue;
    }
    if (markdownValue === mountEcho) return false;

    hasUserEdited = true;
    return true;
  };
}
EOF

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { createDescriptionEditorGuard } from "./description-editor-guard";

describe("createDescriptionEditorGuard", () => {
  it("treats the editor's first mount emission as an echo, not an edit", () => {
    const isUserEdit = createDescriptionEditorGuard();

    expect(isUserEdit("")).toBe(false);
  });

  it("treats the second identical mount emission as an echo too", () => {
    const isUserEdit = createDescriptionEditorGuard();

    // Measured on a running app: the editor emits twice, ~48ms apart, with the same value.
    expect(isUserEdit("****bold**** and _italic_")).toBe(false);
    expect(isUserEdit("****bold**** and _italic_")).toBe(false);
  });

  it("treats a different value as a user edit", () => {
    const isUserEdit = createDescriptionEditorGuard();
    isUserEdit("");

    expect(isUserEdit("Hello from a real edit")).toBe(true);
  });

  it("keeps reporting edits once the user has started editing", () => {
    const isUserEdit = createDescriptionEditorGuard();
    isUserEdit("");

    expect(isUserEdit("a")).toBe(true);
    expect(isUserEdit("ab")).toBe(true);
    expect(isUserEdit("abc")).toBe(true);
  });

  it("reports clearing the field back to the echoed value as an edit", () => {
    const isUserEdit = createDescriptionEditorGuard();
    isUserEdit("");
    isUserEdit("typed something");

    // Regression guard: an early version returned false here, which silently dropped the user's
    // deletion and left the old description in the form.
    expect(isUserEdit("")).toBe(true);
  });

  it("does not suppress edits that merely start with the echoed text", () => {
    const isUserEdit = createDescriptionEditorGuard();
    isUserEdit("A quick video meeting.");

    expect(isUserEdit("A quick video meeting. Now longer.")).toBe(true);
  });

  it("gives each editor instance its own state", () => {
    const first = createDescriptionEditorGuard();
    const second = createDescriptionEditorGuard();

    first("original");
    first("edited");
    expect(first("anything")).toBe(true);

    // A second event type opened afterwards must still swallow its own mount echo.
    expect(second("its own original")).toBe(false);
  });
});

<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

````markdown
# PR draft — issue #10 (save button enabled with no changes)

**Status: NOT OPENED.** `zach-short` has `pull` only on `CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy` (HANDOFF §Settled),
so the branch cannot be pushed. Park here until write access lands, then open as a **draft PR**
(`agents/rules/quality-pr-creation.md`).

- **Branch:** `fix/issue-10-save-button-no-changes` (off `origin/main`)
- **Title:** `fix: stop the description editor marking an untouched event type as changed (#10)`
- **Base:** `main`
- **Labels to request:** none available to him; ask a maintainer for `run-ci` if CI is wanted.

---

## What does this PR do?

- Fixes #10

Opening an event type for editing left **Save** enabled even though nothing had been touched, and
pressing it wrote a corrupted description back to the database.

The Save button was never the problem. It already guards itself with
`disabled={!formMethods.formState.isDirty}` (`EventTypeLayout.tsx:279`), and that guard works — the
form was genuinely dirty on load.

**Root cause.** The Lexical editor behind the description field calls `setText` twice while it
mounts (measured on a running app: two emissions ~48ms apart, identical), echoing back the value it
was just seeded with. `EventSetupTab` wrote that echo into the form with `{ shouldDirty: true }`.
Because the `md.render` → `turndown` round-trip is lossy, the echoed value often differs from what
is stored, so react-hook-form correctly concluded the form had changed:

| stored description | value in the form after mount, before this PR |
|---|---|
| `NULL` | `""` |
| `**bold** and _italic_` | `****bold**** and _italic_` |

That second row is the part the issue does not mention: `handleSubmit` builds its payload from
`dirtyValues` (`useEventTypeForm.ts:320`, `:410`), so `description` *was* in the payload. Saving an
event type you had not edited silently doubled the asterisks in its description.

**The fix.** Two changes:

1. `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/setup/description-editor-guard.ts` (new) — a small
   guard that answers one question per emission: is this the user editing, or the editor echoing
   its own seed value? It remembers the first emitted value, treats anything equal to it as an echo,
   and latches on the first differing value so every later emission is an edit. The latch matters:
   without it, clearing the description back to the echoed text would be silently dropped.
2. `useEventTypeForm.ts` — `description: eventType.description ?? undefined` becomes `?? ""`. With
   the default no longer `undefined`, emptying the description of an event type that never had one
   returns the form to genuinely clean rather than leaving it dirty against `undefined`.

**Known limitation, deliberately out of scope.** "Edit the description, then edit it back, and the

## What does this PR do?

- Fixes #10

Opening an event type for editing left **Save** enabled even though nothing had been touched, and
pressing it wrote a corrupted description back to the database.

The Save button was never the problem. It already guards itself with
`disabled={!formMethods.formState.isDirty}` (`EventTypeLayout.tsx:279`), and that guard works — the
form was genuinely dirty on load.

**Root cause.** The Lexical editor behind the description field calls `setText` twice while it
mounts (measured on a running app: two emissions ~48ms apart, identical), echoing back the value it
was just seeded with. `EventSetupTab` wrote that echo into the form with `{ shouldDirty: true }`.
Because the `md.render` -> `turndown` round-trip is lossy, the echoed value often differs from what
is stored, so react-hook-form correctly concluded the form had changed:

| stored description | value in the form after mount, before this PR |
|---|---|
| `NULL` | `""` |
| `**bold** and _italic_` | `****bold**** and _italic_` |

That second row is the part the issue does not mention: `handleSubmit` builds its payload from
`dirtyValues` (`useEventTypeForm.ts:320`, `:410`), so `description` *was* in the payload. Saving an
event type you had not edited silently doubled the asterisks in its description.

**The fix.** Two changes:

1. `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/setup/description-editor-guard.ts` (new) — a small
   guard that answers one question per emission: is this the user editing, or the editor echoing
   its own seed value? It remembers the first emitted value, treats anything equal to it as an echo,
   and latches on the first differing value so every later emission is an edit. The latch matters:
   without it, clearing the description back to the echoed text would be silently dropped.
2. `useEventTypeForm.ts` — `description: eventType.description ?? undefined` becomes `?? ""`. With
   the default no longer `undefined`, emptying the description of an event type that never had one
   returns the form to genuinely clean rather than leaving it dirty against `undefined`.

**Known limitation, deliberately out of scope.** "Edit the description, then edit it back, and the
button greys out again" is not achievable while the markdown round-trip stays lossy — `- a` / `- b`
comes back as `*   a` / `*   b`, and a hard line break comes back as `<br>`. That lossiness is a
separate defect and deserves its own issue; this PR stops it dirtying an untouched form and stops
it reaching the database on a no-op save.
